articles.title: Salvage reverse shoulder arthroplasty after failed plate fixation of proximal humeral fractures: Clinical outcomes, complications, and prognostic factors.
articles.authors: Ranieri R, Calamita AG, Delle Rose G, Pavone S, Todeschi M, Savare E, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty for proximal humeral fracture complications following previous plate fixation
articles.outcomes: Clinical scores (Constant score 64%, ASES 65, Subjective Shoulder Value 56), range of motion, complications (34% overall, 21% persistent stiffness), reoperations (10%), revisions (7%), bone resorption (50%)
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacement can improve shoulder function after failed fracture plate surgery, but recovery is moderate and complications are common. Greater bone loss at the tuberosity and weak anterior deltoid muscle predict worse outcomes.

articles.title: Extra-Articular Malunions and Nonunions of the Scapular Body and Neck: A Comparison of Functional Outcomes Before and After Reconstruction.
articles.authors: Cole PA, Xu JL, Huaco AA, LaRoque MC, Winter JD
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic malunion or nonunion of scapular neck and/or body fractures
articles.sample_size: 45 patients with >1-year outcomes (40 with malunion, 5 with nonunion)
articles.outcomes: DASH score improved by mean 30.7 points (p<0.001); forward flexion and abduction range of motion and strength improved significantly; all patients achieved radiographic union; 12 patients required further procedures
articles.take_home: Surgical reconstruction of problematic scapular fractures can substantially improve shoulder function, pain, and disability in patients who develop malunions or nonunions. Results were better when surgery was done earlier (6 weeks to 3 months after injury) compared with delayed reconstruction.

articles.title: Early Postoperative Predictors of Two-Year Satisfaction after Ream and Run Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Levins JG, Yamaguchi JT, Whitson AJ, Matsen FA 3rd, Schiffman CJ, Hsu JE
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study from a prospectively maintained database
articles.population: Young, active patients with glenohumeral arthritis undergoing ream and run arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Shoulder comfort at rest and during sleep at 3 and 6 months postoperatively, and overall satisfaction at 2 years
articles.take_home: Patients who reported shoulder comfort at rest by 3 months after surgery were much more likely to be satisfied at 2 years, and those with comfortable sleep by 6 months were also more likely to be satisfied. These early signs may help predict longer-term success after this type of shoulder surgery.

articles.title: The CPT 22-Modifier at a Single Private-Practice Orthopaedic Institution: Success, Reimbursement, and Financial Burden.
articles.authors: Pfeil AN, Jennewine B, Sketchler B, Cusick MC, Hryc CF, Edwards TB, et al.
articles.population: Surgical claims from a single private-practice orthopaedic group across four subspecialties (adult reconstruction, hand, shoulder, and sports medicine)
articles.sample_size: 18,612 claims over 3 years, of which 2,741 (14.7%) used the CPT 22-modifier
articles.outcomes: Success rate of 22-modifier approval, reimbursement amount, days to payment, and rebilling rates by payer type and subspecialty
articles.take_home: The 22-modifier to indicate complex surgery was approved in about 72% of cases overall, but approval rates varied by insurance type and surgical specialty, payments were delayed significantly, and the extra reimbursement of 7.7% may not justify the additional administrative burden.
